claims.finding: Director Homer John Livingston III bought 26,343 shares in the open market at $18.75 on 2026-07-16 - one of three Form 4s filed that evening - and the corpus shows the market did not register it until a retail post on 2026-08-29, six weeks later, by which time the stock was 9% below his purchase price and the company had raised equity at $21 on the 424B5s of 2026-07-07 and 2026-07-08, leaving both the insider and the placement book underwater at the $17.08 pre-print close.
claims.why_not_priced: The Form 4 sat unremarked for six weeks in a corpus that is otherwise saturated with retail attention - 175 captured items, five stored bodies, hundreds of messages - which is direct evidence of non-transmission rather than an assumption about it. The consequence the market has not drawn is a balance-sheet one: the company completed its financing in July, so the cash-runway question that has driven this name's prints is off the table for this one, and the stock is nonetheless 24.09% lower over twenty sessions with no company filing since 2026-07-21 and no news item in the capture. The signed direction is modest and the band wide because the corpus is equally clear about the bear case: the only order on the books is a 30 MW deposit from a newly formed counterparty (FIT Energy), there is no binding Tier-1 data-centre off-take, an S-3ASR shelf remains effective so a further raise is available, and the retail base is openly capitulating.
claims.independence: A separate corpus item points the same way on flow rather than insiders: a reported 114,000-share after-hours block worth about $1,975,000 on 2026-08-31, in docs/72990000fa4f53ff2e17acbdc0a606e7df0a9bc8.txt (message of 2026-09-01T03:44:10Z). It is retail-reported and unverifiable, which is why it is corroboration and not the finding. Pulling the other way, from a third source: https://www.merlintrader.com/fuelcell-energy-stock-hub/ (2026-08-31) frames the quarter as the 'Siemens and the AI data center pivot' with no contract to show.
